newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan cosmetics maker to strengthen Asia business.
newsitem.headline: Japan cosmetics maker to strengthen Asia business.

text.p: Japanese cosmetics maker Mandom Corp is aiming to promote its business in Southeast Asia and is opening a manufacturing base in China to tap the growing market there for beauty products.

Mandom specialises in affordable lines of cosmetics rather than luxury items and has kept its focus on Asia, unlike bigger cosmetics firms Shiseido and Kanebo, whose products are well-known in Europe and the United States.

Mandom vice president Norimoto Asagiri said in an interview with Reuters this week that the company will continue to strengthen its Southeast Asian operations, with the expansion of facilities at its unit PT Tancho Indonesia.
Asagiri is also president of PT Tancho, the company's key unit outside Japan. The company sees the Indonesian unit and the planned facilities in China as its strategic bases outside Japan, he said.
"Our operations in Southeast Asia have 40 years of history and we have no plans to enter European and American markets," Asagiri said. "We will strengthen our business mainly in Southeast Asia."

He said construction of a second plant at PT Tancho was due to start by the end of this year. He also said Mandom plans to start production in China of toiletries, cosmetics and household products next year for direct sales to the potentially huge Chinese market.

He said PT Tancho is expected to post a net profit of 18.3 billion rupiah ($7.71 million) in the year to December 1997, up from an actual net profit of 17 billion rupiah ($7.16 million) the previous year. It sells products under the Tancho brand name rather than Mandom.

In 1997, PT Tancho is expected to post sales of 165 billion rupiah ($69.59 million) and its earnings per share is expected to be 700 rupiah (29.52 cents), he said. PT Tancho's sales were 141.5 billion rupiah ($59.67 million) in 1996, with its earnings per share at 600 rupiah (25.30 cents), he said.
"Our target is to increase earnings per share (at PT Tancho) by 100 rupiah every year," Asagiri said.

Asagiri said that PT Tancho's second plant would cost about 20 billion rupiah ($8.43 million) and that a listing on the newly established foreign section of the Osaka Securities Exchange would be one option for raising the funds.
Currently there are no foreign companies listed there so PT Tancho could be first to list if it went ahead.

But Asagiri said there were some issues standing in the way of such a listing that would need to be looked at. These included the high cost of such a listing in Osaka and Indonesian government regulations, he said, without elaborating on the latter problem.
"It would be costly to list (PT Tancho) shares in Osaka and it would be cheaper to finance (the move) in Singapore under current conditions," he said.

Combined net profits at Mandom's seven overseas units, including PT Tancho, totalled about one billion yen ($8.1 million) in 1996, up 65 percent on a year-on-year basis, on sales of about 9.37 billion yen ($76.8 million), up 25 percent year on year, Asagiri said.
Mandom's buoyant overseas performance contrasts with its domestic earnings, which have been hurt by an increase in unsold stock being returned from shops.
Nomura Securities revised its forecast on Wednesday for Mandom's parent earnings for the year to March 1997.

It said the firm's parent current profits would be 2.8 billion yen ($22.9 million) against a previous forecast of 3.4 billion yen ($27.8 million). Unlike PT Tancho, the parent company follows an April-March fiscal year. Current profit is pre-tax and includes losses or gains on investments.

The new Chinese plant in Guangdong province would be Mandom's last major overseas production centre under current plans, Asagiri said. The sales target in China is 845 million yen ($6.92 million) in calendar 1998, rising to 1.50 billion yen ($12.2 million) in 2000.

Mandom currently sells Indonesian-made products in Vietnam and Burma and might enter the Indian market as well, Asagiri said. In Japan, which is still its main market, Mandom sells cosmetics through supermarkets and convenience stores. ($1=2,371 rupiah, $1=122 yen)
